lessons.title: 16.1 Bone and cartilage
lessons.content:
## Learning outcomes
Explain bone and cartilage and relate its structure or mechanism to biological function.

Bone is mineralised connective tissue; cartilage is more flexible. Osteoblasts build bone, osteoclasts resorb it and osteocytes maintain it.

**Apply your learning:** Use a labelled diagram, sequence or comparison to explain the concept. Consider how a change in one component affects the whole biological system.

explanations.ur: ہڈی معدنیات والی مربوط بافت ہے جبکہ غضروف زیادہ لچکدار ہوتا ہے؛ آسٹیوبلاسٹ ہڈی بناتے، آسٹیوکلاسٹ اسے توڑتے اور آسٹیوسائٹ برقرار رکھتے ہیں۔

lessons.title: 16.2 Human skeleton
lessons.content:
## Learning outcomes
Explain human skeleton and relate its structure or mechanism to biological function.

The axial skeleton supports and protects the central body; the appendicular skeleton includes limbs and their girdles for movement.

**Apply your learning:** Use a labelled diagram, sequence or comparison to explain the concept. Consider how a change in one component affects the whole biological system.

explanations.ur: محوری ڈھانچا جسم کے مرکزی حصے کو سہارا اور حفاظت دیتا ہے؛ ضمیمی ڈھانچے میں بازو، ٹانگیں اور ان کے جوڑنے والے حصے شامل ہیں۔

lessons.title: 16.4 Skeletal disorders and injuries
lessons.content:
## Learning outcomes
Explain skeletal disorders and injuries and relate its structure or mechanism to biological function.

Osteoporosis reduces bone strength; arthritis affects joints. Fractures, sprains and dislocations require appropriate assessment and care.

**Apply your learning:** Use a labelled diagram, sequence or comparison to explain the concept. Consider how a change in one component affects the whole biological system.

lessons.title: 16.5 Muscle contraction
lessons.content:
## Learning outcomes
Explain muscle contraction and relate its structure or mechanism to biological function.

Skeletal muscle contracts when actin and myosin filaments slide past one another using ATP and calcium-dependent regulation.

**Apply your learning:** Use a labelled diagram, sequence or comparison to explain the concept. Consider how a change in one component affects the whole biological system.
